What this is

Human Risk & Impersonation Defense

Human Risk & Impersonation Defense maps every business process that depends on recognizing a person: payment approval, vendor detail changes, executive requests, digital onboarding and helpdesk resets. It covers the full range of impersonation, from a convincing email to a cloned voice or video. We test those processes under controlled conditions and document the control gaps in a form a supervisor or auditor will accept.

Questions We Are Asked

What is impersonation defense?
It is the set of controls that keeps a business process working correctly when an attacker can convincingly imitate a person by voice, video, or document. The defense is mostly procedural (out-of-band verification, independent approval and a fast escalation route), with detection technology used where the process cannot carry the load alone.
Do you simulate deepfake attacks against our staff?
Within written rules of engagement, yes. Named individuals are impersonated only with their written consent, no customer is targeted, and no live payment is moved. The objective is to observe whether the control operates, not to demonstrate that people can be fooled.
Which processes are most exposed?
In most organizations, vendor and payroll bank-detail changes, payment exception release, and helpdesk credential reset carry the majority of the exposure. Digital onboarding carries the regulatory exposure, because the assessment of injection attacks against liveness checks is frequently undocumented.
Does this cover onboarding and eKYC?
Yes, where remote identity verification is in scope. The engagement assesses how the process handles presentation attacks and injected video streams, and whether the assessment and its result are documented well enough to satisfy a supervisor.
Do we need detection technology?
Sometimes. The engagement produces evaluation criteria before it produces a recommendation, and several of the most valuable findings are procedural changes that cost nothing. Technology is proposed where a process cannot be made safe by design alone.
